title: We affirm both sides of the question; most Ubiquitarians deny the Lutheran duty
pass_a_gloss: We affirm both parts of the question. But most of the Ubiquitarians have denied the latter — that Lutherans ought to receive the Reformed as brethren and partners — by sorrowful experience; except those we have praised in the Catallactic Protheoria, from pages 334, 335, 343, 344, and so on.
pass_b_english: Yet most Ubiquitarians have refused the second half — that Lutherans ought to receive the Reformed as brethren and partners — as sorrowful experience shows.
The exceptions are those we have already praised in the Catallactic Protheoria (pp. 334–335, 343–344, and following).
source_text: Affirmamus utrumque; Negarunt autem posterius Ubiquit. plerique, luctuosâ experientiâ; exceptis quos in Protheoria Catallacticâ laudavimus, à pag. 334. 335. 343. 344. &c.
notes: Controv. print p. 76. Verdict + Ubiquitarian refusal; cross-ref Protheoria.

choices.why: ablative of manner/cause from lived schism
